subject: Outbound Gatekeeper & IP Quarantine — Acme Health private endpoint review
messages:
From: Acme Health NetOps <acme-health-netops@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint egress — quarantine behavior & static IP constraints

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this. We're validating how Redwood's private endpoint will behave when our on‑prem workloads attempt outbound connections to unknown external IPs. Two specific asks:

1) Can Redwood support a "quarantine" egress pool (i.e., route unknown destinations to a small, dedicated NAT set that returns TCP RST / ICMP unreachable but still emits logs/alerts)? We need to show our security team the mechanism for capturing unexpected outbound connections.

2) Our firewall is strictly IP allowlist only. We need a stable list of outbound egress IPs (and change windows) your private deployment will use — ideally one per environment (prod/stage). If you rotate, what notice window and delta IPs do you provide?

I've attached a small sample of our monitoring output that shows the unknown destination spike last week.

Attachment: outbound-ip-evidence-20270410.csv (csv)

Appreciate a short runbook or configuration steps we can give to our SOC.

Best,
Mike Donovan
NetOps Manager — Acme Health
acme-health-netops@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Acme Health NetOps <acme-health-netops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — quarantine behavior & static IP constraints

Mike — thanks for the clarity and the logs. Short answer: yes, we can support a quarantined outbound path plus a stable allowlist for your firewalls, but there are tradeoffs (cost, observability model, and how we handle TLS).

I'm looping Ben (sales/solutions) for commercial/notice windows and Laura (infra) for the exact runbook and NAT config. High-level proposal:

- One dedicated egress pool per environment (prod/stage).
- A smaller "quarantine" NAT pool that unknown/blocked destinations are routed to; it returns a deterministic blocked response while emitting detailed audit logs and alerting on destinations not previously seen.
- Rotation policy: monthly by default, with a 14‑day notification for any IP set changes for prod. Can do quarterly rotation for lower churn.

Attached: a draft egress policy that outlines options (we'll finalize after infra signs off).

Attachment: egress-policy-draft-20270409.pdf (pdf)

Ben/Laura — can you confirm the runbook items below and call out required firewall rules? Also, any telemetry/export we should provide to Acme's SOC (Splunk/LogRhythm)?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Mike / Marissa,

Quick commercial/operational notes:

- Dedicated egress pools are covered under the Private plan (we'll include one static / small CIDR per environment). If you require zero IP movement, we can offer an allocation with a longer notice window as a paid option.
- The quarantine pool is treatable as a separate SKU because it requires additional monitoring and alerting hooks — we'll include SOC exports (Syslog/Splunk HTTP event collector) as part of the package.

Operationally:
- We will provide a primary static set for production (3 public IPs) and a quarantine set (2 public IPs) by default. If you need >3, we can size per throughput.
- Rotation windows: default monthly with 14-day heads-up. For paid stability option: quarterly rotation or on‑demand with 30‑day notice.

Deliverables we'll provide once infra signs off:
- CSV of current egress IPs and CIDRs; IP rotation schedule.
- Splunk/SEIM endpoint + sample JSON schema for events.
- A short-run firewall checklist you can hand to your firewall team.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Acme Health NetOps <acme-health-netops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — quarantine behavior & static IP constraints

Hi Mike / team — following up with an actionable runbook and firewall rule set you can hand to your SOC/firewall operators. We've tested the pattern in two customer POCs; notes below reflect that operational experience.

1) Top level architecture (private deployment):
- Customer VPC/subnet -> Private Endpoint (Redwood Private) -> NAT gateway(s) managed by Redwood runtime
- Two NAT pools exported to the public internet per environment:
  * Primary egress pool (prod): 3 public IPs, used for allowlist traffic.
  * Quarantine pool (prod-quarantine): 2 public IPs, used for unknown/blocked destinations.

2) Quarantine behavior:
- Outbound rules in the runtime evaluate destination against an allowlist and recent destination cache. Unknown destinations are stamped and routed to the quarantine pool which immediately drops/actively rejects the traffic (TCP RST / ICMP unreachable).
- Quarantined flows are logged with full 5‑tuple + TLS SNI when available; logs are pushed to your Splunk HEC endpoint or syslog collector in near real time (within 15s).
- Alerts: configurable thresholds (default: >5 unique quarantined destinations within 10min triggers SOC notice).

3) Firewall configuration checklist (provide to your firewall team):
- Allow outbound TCP/UDP from your app subnets to the 5 public IPs we provide.
- Ports allowed: 80, 443, 53 (UDP for DNS); we recommend egress DNS to your existing resolvers only.
- If you have strict TLS inspection policies, note that we rely on TLS SNI and source IP mapping; we do not perform TLS MITM in default deployments.

4) IP rotation & change management:
- We'll give a CSV with current IP allocations and an RFC-like change notice. Default cadence: monthly rotation; 14 days notice.
- For customers needing stricter stability, choose quarterly rotation or dedicated static assignment (30‑day change window) as a commercial add-on.

5) Audit & evidence for compliance:
- Example event (fields): timestamp, src_ip, src_port, dst_ip, dst_port, proto, action (quarantined|allowed), tls_sni, rule_id, tenant_id.
- We'll provide a 90‑day retention export to your Splunk HEC on request (longer retention as an add‑on).

6) Implementation tasks and owners:
- Redwood infra (Laura) — provide final IP CSV, configure quarantine pool, enable Splunk HEC forwarder (ETA 3 business days after approval).
- Redwood account (Marissa) — finalize contract addendum for quarantine SKU and notice cadence.
- Acme NetOps — add provided IPs to firewall allowlist and confirm rule test results.

Next steps: I'll drop the runbook file in the shared drive and push the final CSV after we get approval to provision. Attaching a short markdown runbook.

Attachment: quarantine-runbook-20270411.md (md)

Laura Bennett
Director, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
